newsitem.title: USA: Calif local governments join tobacco fight.
newsitem.headline: Calif local governments join tobacco fight.

text.p: Local governments in California have joined San Francisco in suing major tobacco companies to try to recover the costs of treating smoking-related illnesses, attorneys said Friday.
The move comes as tobacco companies are fighting similar suits by 14 U.S. states.
In June, San Francisco became the first local government in the United States to sue the tobacco industry when it filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court.
On Friday, San Francisco Deputy City Attorney Elizabeth Laporte said the suit was amended to add 10 counties and one more city in California.
The lawsuit, which seeks unspecified damages, was aimed at stopping certain marketing practices by tobacco companies like the alleged targeting of ads to minors.

If successful, the tobacco companies, which include Brown & Williamson Corp., American Tobacco Co. and its parent, B.A.T Industries Plc., Philip Morris Cos. Inc., and R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp., could be forced to pay hundreds of millions of dollars, Laporte said.

The suit, filed under state consumer protection statutes, was also looking for the tobacco companies to give up profits. The complaint could also include a disgorgement of tobacco sales statewide, Laporte said.
Other defendants were Brooke Group Ltd.'s Liggett Group Inc., Loews Corp.'s Lorillard Tobacco Co., the Council for Tobacco Research and the Tobacco Institute.
A Brown & Williamson spokesman said: "The addition of plaintiffs doesn't add any more weight to the basic arguments in the case.

"We don't believe, at the end of the day, that the courts will allow the cities or municipalities to bypass traditional product liability law. We're going to vigorously defend this lawsuit and ultimately we believe we're going to prevail."
The other tobacco companies were not immediately available for comment.

The 10 counties who joined San Francisco in filing the amended suit in the U.S. District Court were Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Mateo, Santa Barbara, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz and Shasta.
She said a second lawsuit was also filed by San Francisco in Superior Court. It included San Francisco, the 10 counties in the other complaint, and the city of San Jose.
San Francisco's federal court suit alleged the tobacco companies suppressed and concealed information about the health consequences of cigarette smoking.
The suits seek orders requiring the companies to stop the alleged targeting of youths in their advertising and to make public their research on smoking addiction and health.
